Fact.Name: Penalty on early withdrawal of savings (Schedule 1 line 18)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 62(a)(9) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/62#a_9) allows, above the line, "The deductions allowed by section 165 for losses incurred in any transaction entered into for profit, though not connected with a trade or business, to the extent that such losses include amounts forfeited to a bank, mutual savings bank, savings and loan association, building and loan association, cooperative bank or homestead association as a penalty for premature withdrawal of funds from a time savings account, certificate of deposit, or similar class of deposit." Schedule 1 (Form 1040) 2026 draft, line 18: "Penalty on early withdrawal of savings". i1040 (2025) p. 95, Line 18: "The Form 1099-INT or Form 1099-OID you received will show the amount of any penalty you were charged." The deduction is the sum of 1099-INT box 2 across all interest reports. There is no dollar threshold and no cap at the interest reported in box 1: 62(a)(9) limits the deduction only to the amount forfeited. Form 1099-OID is not an input in the app (listed under unsupported income sources), so box 3 of a 1099-OID never reaches this line.

Fact.Name: 1099-INT includes interest received as a nominee
Fact.Description: Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf (SHA-256 b92f31ece57a82ea576ac96507fe5df637dbda7489a80eb28aaab88e7c87b287) p. 1, General Instructions: "Use Schedule B (Form 1040) if any of the following applies." The 2026 draft https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sb--dft.pdf (SHA-256 94d34f2eae6ff134bb31b8ba9d5f52961b44e029b1dec2b39db6b62ca5a6a57b) has the same text on PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1) and p. 3. p. 1, General Instructions: "You received interest or ordinary dividends as a nominee." p. 1, Line 1, Nominees: "If you received a Form 1099-INT that includes interest you received as a nominee (that is, in your name, but the interest actually belongs to someone else), report the total on line 1. ... Below this subtotal, enter “Nominee Distribution” and show the total interest you received as a nominee. Subtract this amount from the subtotal and enter the result on line 2."

Fact.Name: 1099-INT includes accrued interest paid to the seller of a bond
Fact.Description: Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf (SHA-256 b92f31ece57a82ea576ac96507fe5df637dbda7489a80eb28aaab88e7c87b287) p. 1, General Instructions: "Use Schedule B (Form 1040) if any of the following applies." The 2026 draft https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sb--dft.pdf (SHA-256 94d34f2eae6ff134bb31b8ba9d5f52961b44e029b1dec2b39db6b62ca5a6a57b) has the same text on PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1) and p. 3. p. 1, General Instructions: "You have accrued interest from a bond." p. 2, Line 1, Accrued interest: "When you buy bonds between interest payment dates and pay accrued interest to the seller, this interest is taxable to the seller. If you received a Form 1099 for interest as a purchaser of a bond with accrued interest, follow the rules earlier under Nominees to see how to report the accrued interest. But identify the amount to be subtracted as “Accrued Interest.”"

Fact.Name: 1099-INT box 3 includes savings bond interest already reported or accrued before the bond was received
Fact.Description: Pub. 550 (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf (SHA-256 83552968a07e63d1c81e5b4f311fc0e54728b5ff9654b5a0d2ba6292c5574317) p. 25, U.S. savings bond interest previously reported: "If you received a Form 1099-INT for U.S. savings bond interest, the form may show interest you do not have to report. ... On Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 1, report all the interest shown on your Form 1099-INT. Then follow these steps. 1. Several rows above Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 2, enter a subtotal of all interest listed on Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 1. 2. Below the subtotal, enter “U.S. Savings Bond Interest Previously Reported” and enter amounts previously reported or interest accrued before you received the bond. 3. Subtract these amounts from the subtotal and enter the result on Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 2." Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf p. 1, Line 1: "Include interest from series EE, H, HH, and I U.S. savings bonds."

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-INT interest that Schedule B Part I subtracts
Fact.Description: #144: any 1099-INT with /interestReports/*/hasScheduleBSubtraction (nominee interest, accrued interest paid to a seller, or U.S. savings bond interest previously reported or accrued before the bond was received). Each is reported in full on Schedule B line 1 and subtracted below a subtotal before line 2; this tool puts the full box 1 and box 3 amounts on Form 1040 line 2b and doesn't produce the subtraction, so the return stops. Cites on the three questions.

Fact.Name: Schedule B required because of taxable interest
Fact.Description: Whether total taxable interest is over $1,500. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 1: "You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends." "Over" is a strict comparison, so exactly $1,500 does not require Schedule B. Compared in whole dollars, the same way as /requiresScheduleBForOrdinaryDividends (income /ordinaryDividends): Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 23, Rounding Off to Whole Dollars: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total."

Fact.Name: Schedule B required because of ordinary dividends
Fact.Description: Whether ordinary dividends (Form 1040 line 3b; Form 1099-DIV box 1a) are over $1,500. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 1: "You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends." Instructions for Schedule B (2025) p. 2, Line 5: "Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends. This amount should be shown in box 1a of your Forms 1099-DIV or substitute statements." Reads income /ordinaryDividends, the whole-dollar total of Form 1099-DIV box 1a (Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 23: "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total"), the same rounding as /requiresScheduleBForInterest.

Whether Schedule B (Form 1040) is required. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 1, General Instructions: "You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends." and "You had a financial interest in, or signature authority over, a financial account in a foreign country or you received a distribution from, or were a grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust." Schedule B (2026 draft) Part III: "You must complete this part if you (a) had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends; (b) had a foreign account; or (c) received a distribution from, or were a grantor of, or a transferor to, a foreign trust." The other listed triggers (seller-financed mortgage interest, accrued interest, OID or bond premium adjustments, Form 8815 exclusion, nominee amounts) are not reported in this return.

Fact.Name: Schedule B Part III questions are answered
Fact.Description: True when Schedule B (Form 1040) line 7a and, when line 7a is "No", line 8 have an answer. A "Yes" on line 7a ends the questions (the rest of line 8 is not asked). An unanswered question is not treated as "No".

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule B Part III foreign account or trust
Fact.Description: Schedule B (2026 draft) Part III: "You must complete this part if you (a) had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends; (b) had a foreign account; or (c) received a distribution from, or were a grantor of, or a transferor to, a foreign trust." Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 2, Line 7a—Question 1: "Check the 'Yes' box even if you aren't required to file FinCEN Form 114." p. 3, Line 7a—Question 2: a U.S. person "must file the form if the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeds $10,000 at any time during 2025" (FinCEN Form 114, 31 U.S.C. 5314). p. 2: "Regardless of whether you are required to file FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR), you may be required to file Form 8938" (26 U.S.C. 6038D). p. 3, Line 8: "If you were the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust that existed during 2025, you may have to file Form 3520" (26 U.S.C. 6048). FinCEN Form 114, Form 8938 and Form 3520 are not computed, so any "Yes" stops the return. The print is refused unless /scheduleBPartIIIAnswered is complete: an unanswered line 7a or line 8 is not "No", including when taxable interest and ordinary dividends are not over $1,500. Exactly $1,500 does not require Schedule B (Instructions for Schedule B (2025) p. 1: "You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends."), and that return prints when every asked Part III question is "No".
